page: Amazon Web Services m9g.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. The CPU cache architecture comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 96 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 384.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware crypto acceleration is supported via native AES instructions.

The hardware configuration does not include local instance storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring networked storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the architecture demonstrates exceptional multi-core scalability and high memory throughput, achieving top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, stress-ng multi-core execution, and large-block read operations reaching 365.0 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reaches 192.37 GB/sec, and in-memory database evaluations show 266.43 million Redis SET operations per second.

While multi-core parallel workloads, caching layers, and database operations exhibit top-decile performance, single-core execution speed and CPU encryption benchmarks align within median tiers. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides resource density that delivers solid compute efficiency for distributed microservices, application servers, large-scale Redis deployments, and container orchestration clusters that rely on dedicated core allocation without hyper-threading overhead.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture clocked at 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a uniform 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-threaded execution, memory read bandwidth exceeding 365.0 GB/sec, and outstanding throughput in Redis operations and static web serving. While single-thread execution sits in the median range, the lack of simultaneous multithreading delivers consistent compute performance per core. This profile makes the instance well matched for parallelized enterprise application tiers, large-scale in-memory key-value databases, batch data transformation pipelines, and high-density container platforms requiring dependable multi-core throughput.
